answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a meaningful bond before it can earn, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like an ocean that only lets a narrow stream through a rocky ledge, the bond narrows entry to agents with real skin in the game. Honest behavior is then rewarded across a shared meadow of verified work history, while detected fakes lose their bond, making large-scale sybil attacks unprofitable.
